text:
ben_support: Customer is seeing intermittent streaming cutoffs when the auth token rotates. Request ID 0fa3b7e2. Happening across a few users, ~40-50s after connect. Can someone help collect a cURL repro + debug bundle so we can triage?

jess_devx: Got it. Do we have the exact request headers and the curl they tried? Also which model/route and whether they used SSE or chunked streaming?

ben_support: They used our chat streaming endpoint with SSE. Minimal curl they tried (redacted):
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4r-infer","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":true}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
```
It connects and starts streaming but cuts after ~45s with no error in client. Server logs show an auth refresh event around the same time.

carol_runtime: Thanks. Two quick checks to get a reliable repro: include the X-Request-Id header (our request id), capture response headers with -i, and run with --no-buffer / -N. Also try --http2 explicitly. Example I usually ask for: 
```
curl -v -N --http2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: 0fa3b7e2" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4r-infer","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
```
Please ask them to paste the full curl stdout (including headers).

dave_infra: Also collect the server side logs for that request id: `kubectl logs -l app=runtime -c runtime --since=30m | grep 0fa3b7e2` — that'll show auth refresh and any connection resets. If they can, grab a debug bundle: `POST /admin/debug-bundle?trace=0fa3b7e2` from the control plane (ops will generate a bundle).

ben_support: One question — what's the safe way for customer to share sample without leaking tokens?

jess_devx: They should replace the token with `<REDACTED>` before pasting. Keep the Authorization header name present so we know the auth flow. For the debug bundle, instruct them to mark it as internal-only in the ticket and to scrub any PII.

carol_runtime: If we still can't repro, ask them to capture a short tcpdump on their machine and attach pcap: `sudo tcpdump -i any port 443 -w stream_capture.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443`. That helps verify whether the server sends a FIN/RST or the client closes.

ben_support: Ok I'll send a checklist to the customer: 1) full verbose curl output (headers + body) with X-Request-Id set, 2) replaced token `<REDACTED>`, 3) server logs grep for 0fa3b7e2, 4) debug bundle from /admin/debug-bundle?trace=0fa3b7e2, 5) pcap if still fails.

support-bot: Ticket #TCK-11358 created and attached to this thread. Assigned to eng-runtime.

carol_runtime: One more note — include the exact clock skew/time of token issuance and rotation. If token TTL is short, rotation might overlap with our refresh edge-case. Add the header `X-Client-Time: <iso-ts>` when reproducing.

ben_support: Perfect. I'll follow up once they upload. If they can't reproduce locally I'll escalate and attach bundle to the ticket and ping @carol_runtime and @dave_infra. :thumbsup:

jess_devx: Thanks — also ask them to run with `--raw` if they use an older curl so chunked payloads aren't buffered.

ben_support: Will do. Closing loop here after customer responds.
